sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed 2.5D city dioramas and near-overhead orthographic circuit workbench
sourceInformation.tech: Full my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (local native Shell focus fix); AI Hub protocol 1 / client 1.4.0; PeerJS 1.5.5; JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Canvas 2D and Web Audio.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original native pixel-rendered green PCBs, cyan traces, patterned components, municipal response crew and warm/cool city lighting
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid rigs, tweens, particles, animated cutter jaws, joint flow and state-driven tool motion.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized electronic score, effects and two filtered gibberish radio voices; music default 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 cooperative technicians: authoritative Hub shared-world dispatch or standalone secure PeerJS Cloud / WebRTC rooms, board claims, shared evidence, crew votes, crew replay and snapshot rejoin. Arbitrary NAT/TURN connectivity is unknown.
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless tests and visual screenshots allowed. Used native deterministic advance, ordinary-input campaign, emulated standard pad, phone/tablet profiles, offline audio, real two-page WebRTC, official Hub harness, and Chromium/Firefox/WebKit. Physical devices, listening and first-time human pacing are unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Read original Blue Sky Rangers manual and creator-maintained history; inspected original circuit screenshot; inspected engine, Hub and PeerJS primary documentation.

testingFeedback: 21 unique game defects were discovered and fixed; the issue ledger records each check and repair.
3 were critical: board occlusion, Hub ended-state initialization, and a retained code-dial index that could break shorter replays.
Most helpful: the fresh ordinary-input campaign, which exposed code-dial carryover and HUD interception; actual Hub rounds also exposed short-dispatch pacing.
Least helpful: syntax-only checks. They confirmed parsing but could not detect hidden boards, blocked clicks or stale network views.
engineFeedback: Most useful: native shapes/materials, Humanoid rigs, fixed-step headless advance and the shared controller-readable shell.
Yes. Large sorted planes and a background overlay covered the board. Native decals and explicit sorting fixed it.
Built separately: the authoritative repair, evidence, recovery, heat, command validation and cooperative voting model.
Hardest: keeping world projection, native menus, input focus and online fuse time consistent.
Changed one native Shell.show focus-retention path: refreshing a screen now preserves its focused widget. The full gamepad practice disposal verifies it.
Add a documented interactive-board surface with projected, selectable terminal anchors.
promptFeedback: Most useful: the source-specific repair loop, exact artifact contract and requirement for real-input acceptance.
Confusing: PLAN.md names a different model effort/context; the filled TASK.md supplies the actual run metadata.
Hardest: integrating repair recovery, deduction, native presentation and two complete networking lifecycles.
Suggested change: include a machine validator for the filename and exit-report schema in the starting folder.

aiHub.name: Bomb Squad All Wired Up
aiHub.tagline: Keep your nerve. Save the city.
aiHub.description: Repair hazardous circuits, read the hidden digit stencils and make the final disarm call. Three original city cases and a guided workbench support solo play or a cooperative response crew.
aiHub.controls: D-pad/WASD focus; Cross/Space or mouse apply/hold; L1/R1 or 1–4 tools; Square/E test; Triangle/R repeat; R2/Tab evidence; Options/Escape menu; assisted touch.
